title: Free target/produce before verifier; resume retries from kept candidate
summary: Retry of job 20261028-081326-zzxg (failed in planning round 3, unverified): delete the job's target/produce after Athena's checks pass and before the pre-verifier disk gate, and make `athena retry` resume low-disk, usage-limit and interrupted-process stops from the kept candidate at the stopped stage with no planner or producer run. Audience: Athena operators.

defaults_applied.how: All changes and tests are Rust.
New tests plus cargo test, clippy -D warnings, fmt --check.
Fix both the disk gap and the resume gap for all three environment causes.
Criteria check removal and resume happening via tests.
Outcome criterion about 9.5 GB free and non-replanning retry.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt.
CHANGELOG entry and clear test names.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Job 20261028-081326-zzxg findings addressed: (1) criterion 6 fixture must pass the early disk gate (~run/mod.rs:1980): the test free-space reader reports 9.5 GB only when both target/produce and a marker written by the check step exist, else 10.5 GB; (2) interrupted-process cause is planned explicitly: a Dispatched job with no running process, whose work dir and recovered completed producer invocation exist, is kept and resumed at the candidate stage, tied to earlier_attempt_with and recover_interrupted, with a resume_stage unit test; (3) the retry test states the reader agent still runs on ask, asserting reader=1, planner=critic=producer=0, verifier=1; (4) disk::is_environment_reason is widened/reused (usage limit included) instead of adding a near-duplicate, and its callers checked; (5) the low-disk retry test uses a marker file under the state root, not counting free-space reads; (6) timeout_seed is made aware of the resume stage.
Before coding, trace gate order in run/mod.rs (early disk gate, checks, removal, pre-verifier gate) so each test fixture reaches the code under test.
Each new test must fail on the old code and pass on the new.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml) need no change; the 10 GB minimum is unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test in crates/athena-core, whose fixture passes the early disk gate and the checks, shows target/produce is absent after checks pass and before the verifier runs, with the pre-verifier gate passing at 9.5 GB reported before removal. Run: cargo test
A test shows target/produce is still present when a check fails (send-back). Run: cargo test

A test stops a job on low disk (marker file under the state root) before the verifier, removes the marker, runs retry, and asserts reader=1, planner=0, critic=0, producer=0, verifier=1 on the kept candidate. Run: cargo test

A resume_stage unit test shows low disk, usage limit and an interrupted process (Dispatched, no running process, completed recovered producer invocation) after build each resume at the stopped stage from the kept candidate, using the timed-out-producer keep mechanism. Run: cargo test

disk::is_environment_reason in crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs is reused/widened for usage limit rather than a near-duplicate added, and timeout_seed in reading.rs takes the resume stage into account (Grep).
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing both fixes.
Outcome check: a job passing checks with 9.5 GB free no longer stops on disk for lack of target/produce space, and its retry does not re-plan or rebuild; the tests above fail on the old code.

out_of_scope: Changing the 10 GB minimum free-disk threshold
Changing planner/critic round limits or planning checks
departures: Two-part change touching the run pipeline and retry resume, with subtle test fixtures that failed planning before; cost and time are raised and pass probability lowered.
urgent_reason: Cuts wasted time: it stops finished jobs failing on disk and stops retries re-planning and rebuilding for about $5.
hard_reason: Changes the run pipeline (disk gate ordering, what the verifier sees) and how retry resumes jobs, so mistakes are costly and hard to see.
